answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. The design works because cost compounds over compute, time, and reputation, growing faster than the influence the cluster can extract. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds. Consider a nadir as the anchor of the cost.
